passage: Jatin, let old Gopika tell you about my final-year project, since you say your team is "fine". Our best coder, Sameer, was fast. When a task looked slow, he took it: "Let me just do it, it takes ten minutes." By the third week the rest of us were only making tea and formatting slides. Nobody had lied; it simply felt easier. Then came the viva. The examiner pointed at our code and asked Fatima, "How does this module work?" She looked at Sameer. Silence. Sameer answered for her. The examiner smiled kindly and said, "So who built what?" We passed, but I still remember Fatima's face. I learnt that a project you cannot explain is not really yours.

qa.q: Who was the fast coder in Gopika's team?
What was Fatima feeling at the viva when the examiner asked about the module?
qa.a: Fatima was embarrassed and helpless, looking at Sameer in silence because she could not explain the code.

qa.q: What choice inside the story could Sameer have made instead of taking tasks over, and why?
qa.a: Sameer could have explained each task and let a teammate try it, because the others would then understand their own part and could answer at the viva.

qa.q: How did the examiner see the team?
qa.a: The examiner saw a group where one person spoke for everyone, which is why the question 'So who built what?' followed.

grounding: Shows one member taking over a team project so the others lose ownership and cannot explain their own work at the viva.

passage: By October, Yusuf had quietly rewritten most of the team's hospital-queue app. "It's faster if I just do it," he'd say, and push new code at 2 am. Ira and the other two stopped opening the project. Why fix what Yusuf would redo by morning? Then came the complication: the viva, planned for late April, was pulled forward to the first week of April because the external examiner had to travel. There was no time left to catch up. On the day, the examiner pointed at Ira. "Explain how your app decides the queue order." Ira looked at the screen. She had written the first version of that logic in August. None of it was left. "I think... Yusuf changed it." The examiner turned to the other two, who also looked at Yusuf. Yusuf explained it perfectly. The examiner wrote: "Only one member understands the project."

qa.q: When was the viva moved to?
qa.a: To the first week of April.

qa.q: What was Ira feeling when asked to explain?
qa.a: Ira felt lost and embarrassed, since the logic she once wrote had been completely replaced.

qa.q: What would you change first in how Yusuf worked?
qa.a: Yusuf could explain each change in short team sessions or pair with a teammate on each module, so everyone keeps ownership and understanding.

qa.q: How might Yusuf feel reading the examiner's note?
qa.a: Yusuf may feel uneasy that taking over, meant to help, left the whole team marked down.

grounding: Shows the strongest coder taking over instead of explaining, so teammates lose ownership and cannot explain their own project at an earlier-than-planned viva.

passage: In a Chennai college's project lab, Pankaj had the fastest fingers anyone had seen. When Chandrika's database design had a flaw in September, he fixed it overnight, and redesigned it while he was at it. When the map screen lagged, he rewrote it. By December the team's e-waste pickup app was ninety percent his code. Chandrika kept writing the report, describing features she hadn't touched. She told herself it was fine; the app worked, and it looked beautiful. At the viva in April, the examiner asked her, "Why did you choose this table structure?" Chandrika opened her mouth. It was no longer her structure. "Pankaj changed it," she said, and felt her face burn. The examiner asked the third member about the map. Same answer. Pankaj, sitting at the end, looked at his hands. Their marks came back uneven, and the report was flagged for review.

qa.q: How much of the app was Pankaj's code by December?
How did Chandrika feel at the viva?
qa.a: Chandrika felt ashamed, her face burning, unable to explain a structure that was no longer hers.

qa.q: What else could the team have done in September?
qa.a: They could have agreed that Pankaj reviews and explains fixes instead of rewriting, so Chandrika keeps ownership of the database.

qa.q: How might Pankaj feel at the end of the viva?
qa.a: Pankaj seems uneasy, looking at his hands, perhaps realising that doing everything left his teammates unable to speak for their own project.

grounding: Illustrates the strongest coder rewriting teammates' parts instead of explaining, so at the viva the others cannot explain the project.
